test_title: Delhi Police Constable (Executive) 2023 - GK/CA (Held on: 16 Nov, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: gk
question:
Arrange the following Fundamental Duties in sequential order according to their mention in the Constitution of India.

A. To abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions.

B. To uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India.

C. To cherish and follow the noble ideals which inspired our national struggle for freedom.

D. To safeguard public property and to abjure violence.
solution:
The correct answer is __**3) A, C, B, D**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• **To abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions** is the first fundamental duty listed in Article 51A of the Constitution of India.

• **To cherish and follow the noble ideals which inspired our national struggle for freedom** is the second fundamental duty mentioned in the Constitution.

• **To uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India** is the third fundamental duty listed in the Constitution.

• **To safeguard public property and to abjure violence** is the fourth fundamental duty mentioned in the Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Fundamental Duties**:

• The Fundamental Duties are a set of moral obligations mentioned in Part IVA (Article 51A) of the Constitution of India. These duties are expected to be performed by every citizen of India to uphold the spirit of patriotism and to support the unity and integrity of the nation.

• Originally, the Constitution of India did not contain these duties. They were added by the 42nd Amendment Act in 1976, upon the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee.

• There are currently 11 Fundamental Duties listed in the Constitution, which emphasize the importance of respect for the Constitution, the National Flag and the National Anthem, and the promotion of harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood among all the people of India.

• Although these duties are non-justiciable, they serve as moral guidelines for the citizens and play a significant role in the governance of the country.

• **Article 51A**:

• Article 51A of the Indian Constitution specifically deals with Fundamental Duties. It outlines the duties that every citizen of India is expected to follow to contribute positively to the nation.

• This article was inserted by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976, and it lists 10 duties initially, with an 11th duty added by the 86th Amendment Act, 2002.

• The duties mentioned under Article 51A reflect the importance of adherence to the Constitution, promotion of harmony, protection of the environment, and the development of scientific temper, among others.
